title: Turn 8, Gishath resolving, two blue seats passed: swing now on one free trick, or untap into the covered line?

board.you: Turn 8, precombat main. Battlefield: eight lands including Rogue's Passage and Secluded Courtyard (naming Dinosaur), Boros Signet, Drover of the Mighty, Pantlaza, Sun-Favored. Nine mana was available; Gishath, Sun's Avatar was cast from the command zone for eight (first cast — no tax) and is on the stack with one mana still open. Rogue's Passage's {4} activation is NOT affordable this turn.

opponents.board: four untapped lands (two produce blue), a 2/4 wall, drew two extra cards last turn. Stated archetypal assumption: holds a sorcery-speed wrath and one counterspell.
two Islands open, two 3/3 fliers. Passed on Gishath.
empty — swept by Seat A last turn; fully tapped out.

scenario.mana_available: {G} (Drover) after paying for Gishath; Flawless Maneuver is castable for free once Gishath resolves (you control a commander)

stack.object: Gishath, Sun's Avatar (cast from the command zone)
stack.note: Both blue seats have passed priority — the counterspell window on the commander itself is closing. Gishath will resolve with haste, vigilance, trample. The table has not seen Flawless Maneuver; nobody knows whether you hold protection.

extras.context: The table read: your mana has been visible all game — goldfish mean cast turn is 7.969, median 8, so every experienced opponent expected the commander THIS turn and Seat A's held wrath is priced for it. Your protection is unknown information: the deck holds a board trick by turn 6 in only 48.5% of goldfish games, so the table cannot assume you have one.
extras.assumption: Seat A wraths at sorcery speed on their own turn when it maximizes value; the held counterspell is now earmarked for a protection spell or a follow-up threat, not the already-resolving commander.

scenario.question: Gishath resolves. Do you attack Seat C's empty board immediately with Flawless Maneuver as your only cover, hold Gishath home and untap into a covered Rogue's Passage swing, or attack Seat A to pressure the wrath-holder?

branches.choice: Swing at Seat C now — Flawless Maneuver is the cover
branches.line: Declare Gishath attacking Seat C and don't look back. The lane is wide open — no blockers, no untapped mana — and haste makes the cast-turn attack legal. Seven damage connects, seven cards flip, and the payoff banks before anyone untaps. Then hold the free Flawless Maneuver through the entire next rotation: it costs zero mana while your commander is on the battlefield, so Seat A's wrath turn walks straight into indestructible.
branches.signals: Casting AND connecting in one turn promotes you to archenemy on the spot — accept the promotion, because the trigger's payoff (bodies, draws, a discover) is banked before anyone gets a wrath window. Your lone floating {G} and the 'attacking with no protection open' look practically beg for the wrath. Let them believe it. That read is exactly wrong, and Maneuver is how you cash their mistake.
branches.coalition_risk: Real, and priced in: hitting the seat that just got swept reads as bullying the weak player, and Seats A and B start coordinating next rotation. Fine by you — one attack just converted into a board plus cards, and resources banked now are resources that survive whatever the coalition brings.
branches.coaching: This is the pivot window, and closers take it the turn it opens. The counter window on Gishath shut when both blue seats passed, the open lane exists RIGHT NOW and closes when Seat C untaps and redeploys, and your cover is free. Run the recast math and the answer only gets clearer: Selvala, Heart of the Wilds and Regal Behemoth make a 10-mana recast genuinely reachable — Selvala taps for X equal to your greatest power, and Gishath himself makes that 7, while Behemoth doubles your land taps under the crown — but 'reachable' still burns the tempo turn and re-arms every held answer. Cover is strictly cheaper than recasting; that is the whole ballgame. Know Maneuver's limits — it beats destruction, not exile or bounce — and destruction is precisely what the stated assumption says Seat A is holding. Swing, bank the trigger, and start your reign as archenemy with the resources to enjoy it.

citations.quote: If a creature has haste, it can attack even if it hasn’t been controlled by its controller continuously since their most recent turn began.
A commander cast from the command zone costs an additional {2} for each previous time the player casting it has cast it from the command zone that game.

branches.choice: Hold Gishath home — untap into Rogue's Passage plus open protection
branches.line: Resolve Gishath, attack with nobody, and pass with vigilant blockers up. Next turn, on ten mana, activate Rogue's Passage in the declare attackers step — before blocks, because evasion gained after a legal block is declared does not undo the block — guaranteeing a full 7-card reveal with Maneuver still free behind it.
branches.signals: A resolved 7/6 commander standing still is still the loudest object on the battlefield — you inherit the full archenemy signal and bank exactly nothing for it. Seat A now schedules the wrath at their leisure, into a board that gained zero.
branches.coalition_risk: Highest of the three, wearing a disguise: 'patience' hands the wrath-holder a free rotation to answer you at maximum value and gives Seats B and C a turn to redeploy blockers and countermagic. It reads as safety. It functions as a gift.
branches.coaching: I respect discipline — so let's audit what this discipline actually buys. Passage's guarantee is insurance against blockers, and Seat C has NO blockers this turn: you would be paying a full rotation to insure a risk that does not currently exist while the risk that does exist — the sorcery-speed wrath — compounds. The pivot-window rule says every held answer arrives the moment the 8-drop is on the table; that clock started when Gishath hit the stack, not when you decide to swing. And here's the kicker: Maneuver is only free WHILE you control your commander. If Seat A answers Gishath on your off-turn, your free trick becomes a 3-mana spell protecting nothing. Don't let Selvala and Regal Behemoth talk you into patience either — a richer untap turn cannot buy back a lane that closed or a trigger that never banked. Save this line for the board where every lane is blocked, and look up: that is not this board.

citations.quote: If an attacking creature gains or loses an evasion ability after a legal block has been declared, it doesn’t affect that block.

branches.choice: Swing at Seat A — pressure the wrath-holder
branches.line: Declare Gishath attacking Seat A, on the theory that the player holding the wrath is the real threat and 7 damage plus the reveal punishes them directly.
branches.signals: Attacking the control seat announces that you've identified the problem — and control seats answer that announcement with mana, not life total. Worse, it tells Seats B and C you'll do their fighting for free, and they will happily let you.
branches.coalition_risk: Low social cost, high strategic cost: your best turn goes into the one seat equipped to make it worthless, while the actually-open lane closes behind you.
branches.coaching: Here's the trap, and I'm naming it before you walk into it: the trigger scales with damage DEALT to a player. Seat A's 2/4 wall chump-blocks, trample forces you to assign 4 lethal to the wall first, and only 3 cross — your reveal shrinks from 7 cards to 3. That's the difference between a board and a body: stack 001's verified cascade — five bodies, three draws, a discover at X=6 — came off a full 7. 'Attack the problem player' is the right instinct pointed at the wrong resource: their life total doesn't beat you, their wrath does, and this line hands that wrath a smaller board to punish. You'll pressure Seat A soon enough — after the trigger banks somewhere it counts.

citations.quote: The controller of an attacking creature with trample first assigns damage to the creature(s) blocking it. Once all those blocking creatures are assigned lethal damage, any excess damage is assigned as its controller chooses among those blocking creatures and the player, planeswalker, or battle the creature is attacking.

recommendation.choice: Swing at Seat C now — Flawless Maneuver is the cover
recommendation.rationale: All three conditions of the pivot window are met, and all three are temporary: the counter window on the commander has closed, the unblocked lane exists this turn only, and your protection costs zero. Holding trades a guaranteed 7-card reveal for insurance against a blocker that does not exist while the wrath you actually fear gets a free turn; attacking the wrath-holder shrinks the reveal to 3 through a chump block. The table has been counting to exactly this turn — goldfish mean cast 7.969, median 8 — and Seat A's wrath is priced for it. Selvala, Heart of the Wilds and Regal Behemoth soften the recast tax without repealing it: an answered commander still costs the tempo turn that cover would have saved. The only surprise you have left is Maneuver. This turn is its maximum leverage — spend it, bank the trigger, and take the throne on your own terms.
